docs.title: vergil-fixture-rust-app
docs.text:
This is a Vergil test fixture. It has no users.

It holds a small Rust command-line application so that Vergil's support for Rust applications runs against a real one: local validation with vrg-validate, CI, the dependency and license audit, this docs site and the tagged release. Each fixture run adds one small increment to the program and drives it through Vergil's full cycle, from change to release.

Why the fixture exists, and how a fixture run works, is set out in the spec of epic vergil-project/.github#1091.

docs.title: What it exercises
docs.text:
• vrg-validate's Rust checks: cargo fmt, cargo clippy, cargo check, tests at 100% line and region coverage with cargo llvm-cov, doctests with cargo test --doc, cargo deny against the fleet's packaged license, advisory and source policy, and the release build (cargo build --release --locked --workspace).
  • Three real runtime dependencies, clap, anyhow and serde_json, for the audit and the dependency tooling to work on.
  • The fleet's CI and CD workflows, this site and the release.

Nothing it builds is published to a package registry.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: The fixture is a Cargo package with one binary, vergil-fixture-rust-app.

docs.title: Build and run
docs.text:
From a clone of the repository:

$ cargo run -- greet Ada
Hello, Ada

cargo build --release puts the binary at target/release/vergil-fixture-rust-app.

docs.title: Validate
docs.text:
As in every Vergil repo, validation runs in the Vergil dev container, and nothing else is the gate:

vrg-container-run -- vrg-validate

docs.title: Layout
docs.text: Path Holds src/main.rs the binary: parse the command line, run, set the exit code src/lib.rs run, which dispatches a parsed subcommand src/cli.rs the clap parser and the Command enum src/commands/ one module per subcommand, with its unit tests tests/cli.rs end-to-end tests that run the built binary

docs.title: Adding a subcommand
docs.text:
A fixture run grows the program by one subcommand at a time, with no restructuring:

  1. Add src/commands/<name>.rs with the subcommand's Args (when it takes any), its logic as a plain function, a run that writes the result, and unit tests.
  2. Declare the module in src/commands.rs.
  3. Add a variant to Command in src/cli.rs, and its arm to the match in run in src/lib.rs.
  4. Add its end-to-end tests to tests/cli.rs, its entry to the Usage page, and its row to the subcommand table in the repository's README.md.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
vergil-fixture-rust-app <COMMAND>
Command Prints greet NAME a greeting for NAME sum [NUMBERS]... the sum of the integers max NUMBERS... the largest of the integers min NUMBERS... the smallest of the integers product [NUMBERS]... the product of the integers range NUMBERS... the largest of the integers less the smallest mean NUMBERS... the mean of the integers, rounded toward zero count [NUMBERS]... how many integers were given median NUMBERS... the median of the integers, rounded toward zero distinct [NUMBERS]... how many different integers were given evens [NUMBERS]... how many of the integers are even mode NUMBERS... the most common of the integers, the smallest on a tie info the program's name and version as JSON

--help prints the commands, and --version prints the program's name and version.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 success 1 the command failed; the reason is on standard error, after error: 2 a usage error, such as a missing command or an argument that does not parse

docs.title: greet
docs.text:
Prints Hello, NAME.

$ vergil-fixture-rust-app greet Ada
Hello, Ada

A name that is empty or only whitespace is an error:

$ vergil-fixture-rust-app greet " "
error: the name must not be blank

docs.title: sum
docs.text:
Prints the sum of its arguments, which are 64-bit signed integers. Negative numbers need no --. With no arguments, the sum is 0.

$ vergil-fixture-rust-app sum 1 2 3
6
$ vergil-fixture-rust-app sum -4 2
-2

A sum outside the 64-bit signed range is an error:

$ vergil-fixture-rust-app sum 9223372036854775807 1
error: the sum overflows a 64-bit signed integer

docs.title: max
docs.text:
Prints the largest of its arguments, which are 64-bit signed integers. Negative numbers need no --.

$ vergil-fixture-rust-app max 1 3 2
3
$ vergil-fixture-rust-app max -4 -2
-2

With no arguments there is no largest number, so it is an error:

$ vergil-fixture-rust-app max
error: max needs at least one number

docs.title: min
docs.text:
Prints the smallest of its arguments, which are 64-bit signed integers. Negative numbers need no --.

$ vergil-fixture-rust-app min 2 1 3
1
$ vergil-fixture-rust-app min -4 -2
-4

With no arguments there is no smallest number, so it is an error:

$ vergil-fixture-rust-app min
error: min needs at least one number

docs.title: product
docs.text:
Prints the product of its arguments, which are 64-bit signed integers. Negative numbers need no --. With no arguments, the product is 1.

$ vergil-fixture-rust-app product 2 3 4
24
$ vergil-fixture-rust-app product -4 2
-8

A product outside the 64-bit signed range is an error:

$ vergil-fixture-rust-app product 9223372036854775807 2
error: the product overflows a 64-bit signed integer

docs.title: range
docs.text:
Prints the spread of its arguments, which are 64-bit signed integers: the largest less the smallest. Negative numbers need no --.

$ vergil-fixture-rust-app range 2 9 3
7
$ vergil-fixture-rust-app range -4 7
11

With no arguments there is no spread, so it is an error:

$ vergil-fixture-rust-app range
error: range needs at least one number

A spread outside the 64-bit signed range is an error:

$ vergil-fixture-rust-app range -9223372036854775808 9223372036854775807
error: the range overflows a 64-bit signed integer

docs.title: mean
docs.text:
Prints the mean of its arguments, which are 64-bit signed integers, rounded toward zero. Negative numbers need no --. The mean lies between the smallest and the largest argument, so unlike a sum it never overflows.

$ vergil-fixture-rust-app mean 2 4 9
5
$ vergil-fixture-rust-app mean -1 -2
-1

With no arguments there is no mean, so it is an error:

$ vergil-fixture-rust-app mean
error: mean needs at least one number

docs.title: count
docs.text:
Prints how many arguments it was given, which are 64-bit signed integers. Negative numbers need no --, and with no arguments it prints 0.

$ vergil-fixture-rust-app count 2 -4 9
3
$ vergil-fixture-rust-app count
0

docs.title: median
docs.text:
Prints the median of its arguments, which are 64-bit signed integers: the middle one once they are sorted, or, for an even count, the mean of the two middle ones, rounded toward zero. Negative numbers need no --, and the median never overflows.

$ vergil-fixture-rust-app median 9 -4 2
2
$ vergil-fixture-rust-app median 8 -4 2 5
3

With no arguments there is no median, so it is an error:

$ vergil-fixture-rust-app median
error: median needs at least one number

docs.title: distinct
docs.text:
Prints how many different integers it was given, which are 64-bit signed integers, counting a repeated value once. Negative numbers need no --, and with no arguments it prints 0.

$ vergil-fixture-rust-app distinct 2 -4 2 9
3
$ vergil-fixture-rust-app distinct
0

docs.title: evens
docs.text:
Prints how many of the integers it was given are even, which are 64-bit signed integers. Negative numbers need no --, so -4 is even, and with no arguments it prints 0.

$ vergil-fixture-rust-app evens 2 -4 7 9
2
$ vergil-fixture-rust-app evens
0

docs.title: mode
docs.text:
Prints the integer it was given most often, of 64-bit signed integers. When several are given equally often, it prints the smallest of them. Negative numbers need no --.

$ vergil-fixture-rust-app mode 2 -4 9 -4
-4
$ vergil-fixture-rust-app mode 9 2 9 2
2

With no arguments it is an error:

$ vergil-fixture-rust-app mode
error: mode needs at least one number

docs.title: info
docs.text:
Prints one line of compact JSON with the program's name and version, the crate's current version from Cargo.toml:

$ vergil-fixture-rust-app info
{"name":"vergil-fixture-rust-app","version":"<VERSION>"}

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• add the Rust CLI program and run CodeQL on it (#4)
  • feat(fixture): a small CLI with greet, sum and info subcommands

The fixture's program: a clap CLI with three subcommands, one module each, unit and end-to-end tests at 100% line coverage, the docs pages and the README. Runtime dependencies: clap, anyhow and serde_json. Epic vergil-project/.github#1091, plan Task 6d.

  • ci(security): run CodeQL on Rust so the required checks report

Remove run-codeql: false so the security job runs CodeQL on Rust. The CI-gates ruleset requires security / codeql and the GHAS CodeQL check, so every PR here was blocked with all checks green.

  • add the max subcommand (#8) max NUMBERS... prints the largest of its integers and fails when none are given. Its logic function carries a doctest, the first in the fixture, so the cargo test --doc step validates a real test. Ref vergil-project/vergil-fixture-rust-app#5

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• add the min subcommand (#24)
  • feat(cli): add the min subcommand

Prints the smallest of its integer arguments, and fails when given none, mirroring max. Tests cover the function, run (success, error and write error), parsing, dispatch and the binary end to end.

  • chore(deps): roll anyhow back to 1.0.103 in Cargo.lock

Fixture run (#20): the lock moves anyhow 1.0.104 -> 1.0.103, inside its declared requirement 1, so the release's dependency update has a guaranteed upgrade to make. Cargo.toml is unchanged. 1.0.103 is the earliest version clear of RUSTSEC-2026-0190, which the cargo-deny audit rejects in 1.0.102.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
• bring region coverage to 100% before the Rust region gate (#19)
  • test(coverage): cover every region

Region coverage was 98.64% (5 of 368 regions missed; lines 100%). Four were the write-error ? of each command's run, and one the unreachable false arm of an unguarded matches! in parses_info. llvm-cov counts a generic function's regions from its best-covered instantiation alone, so every run test now shares one writer type (a bounded byte slice, through commands::testing::capture), and a zero-capacity writer drives the write error. parses_info compares the Debug form instead. No exclusion is added.

  • style(coverage): format the greet run test
